location: apps/web/src/data/deities.json primarySources (468 entries): 91 contain a description, paraphrase or composite in the text field (e.g. sky-woman, raven, dine coyote 'Coyote steals the child... (paraphrase)'); 35 are dated 'Traditional' with no collector (18 of 18 Yoruba, 14 of 14 Polynesian); type PrimarySource in types/Entity.ts:34 has no kind field
problem: Quote fields mix verbatim translations, paraphrases, summaries and uncollected oral text, with nothing in the schema to tell them apart.
impact: Readers and students may cite a paraphrase as a quotation; the 2026-09-18 ledger verified only 35 structured excerpts.
fix: Add kind: 'quotation'|'paraphrase'|'summary'|'oral-tradition' to PrimarySource, backfill the 91+35 entries, render a visible label, and require translator plus edition for any 'quotation'. [Size: ~12h]
verification: Script asserts every primarySource has kind, and every kind=quotation has a translator or edition; run in CI. Re-run counts (should be 0 untyped).

location: apps/web/src/data/deities.json: aztec-pantheon 4/14 and mesoamerican-pantheon 7/17 quotes cite Lewis Spence, The Myths of Mexico and Peru (1913); egyptian-pantheon cites Budge (osiris); stories.json citationSources for haudenosaunee, tlingit-haida and Yoruba mark early-20th-century ethnography and untitled 'Yoruba Oral Tradition'/'Ifa Oral Tradition' as type 'primary'
problem: A 1913 popular retelling and Budge translations stand in as primary texts, and colonial-era ethnographic records (Swanton 1909, Parker, Hewitt) are labelled primary for living traditions.
impact: Scholarly weakness on the pantheons where trust matters most; 'Yoruba Oral Tradition' cannot be checked by a reader.
fix: Replace Spence with Sahagun/Florentine Codex (Anderson and Dibble), Codex or Dibble translations, and Popol Vuh (Tedlock); relabel ethnographic records 'early ethnographic record (recorded by X from Y)'; swap vague oral-tradition citations for named collections (e.g. Wande Abimbola Ifa corpus) or mark as unsourced. [Size: ~10h]
verification: Grep for Spence|Budge returns 0 as primary; new type value 'ethnographic-record' used and rendered.

location: apps/web/src/data/deities.json: anubis detailedBio ('Anubis invented the art of mummification when he helped Isis'), primarySources[0] Plutarch De Iside (dogs led Isis to the child); ganesha detailedBio (beheading and elephant head) vs primarySources[0] Ganapati Atharvashirsha; marduk ('Originally a minor god of thunderstorms'); quetzalcoatl ('opposition to human sacrifice') cited to Spence
problem: In my 15-entry sample, the single cited passage does not appear to support the headline claim for Anubis, Ganesha and Quetzalcoatl (by reading the entries; I did not re-check the cited editions). The Marduk bio says 'Originally a minor god of thunderstorms' (present in deities.json), which I flag as contested but did not verify against a source. Bios carry no inline citations.
impact: Plausible-sounding claims with a mismatched citation are the failure mode a reference site cannot afford; the Anubis and Quetzalcoatl claims are contested or later traditions presented as fact.
fix: Add per-claim footnote markers to detailedBio for the top 50 deities by importanceRank, tying each factual sentence to a source and locator; mark late or contested traditions ('attested in Ptolemaic-era texts'). [Size: ~24h]
verification: For each of the 4 flagged entries a reviewer confirms the claim in the cited locator or the claim is reworded; spot check 20 more.

location: apps/web/src/data/pantheons.json (figuresLabel set for 12 traditions, absent for hindu-pantheon and japanese-pantheon); app/pantheons/[slug]/page.tsx:147,222 (fallback 'Deities'); pantheons.json hindu description 'Hindu mythology...' and japanese name 'Japanese Pantheon' while its text calls Shinto the indigenous spirituality
problem: Hindu and Shinto, both living religions, fall back to 'Deities' and 'Pantheon', while Yoruba, Haudenosaunee, Tlingit-Haida, Diné, Aboriginal and others get custom labels and protocol notes. verification: Grep for hard-coded 'Deity'/'deity' in components/quiz, components/compare returns only labelled-by-data uses; visual check of /pantheons/japanese and /pantheons/hindu.

location: apps/web/src/data/pantheons.json (tlingit-haida, haudenosaunee, dine, aboriginal-australian detailedHistory); no named cultural reviewers on /about or /sources
problem: Entries state protocols well, but no named community review, correction log or consultation is shown anywhere; the support page says 'built by one person'.

location: apps/web/src/lib/spaced-repetition.ts:6-12,73-110 (comment says FSRS; code is an SM-2-style ease-factor scheduler); components/review/FlashCard.tsx:57-80 (flip then self-rate); lib/spaced-repetition.ts:37-42 (5 card types, all recognition or matching)
problem: The scheduler is called FSRS but multiplies interval by an ease factor (SM-2 family), and cards are flip-then-self-rate recognition prompts with no commit-before-reveal step.
impact: Retrieval practice works when learners attempt recall before seeing the answer; recognition-only cards and a mislabelled algorithm give weaker retention and an inaccurate claim.
fix: Rename the comment, or adopt ts-fsrs; add a 'type or tap your answer first' step with 3 confidence levels; add 'why' and 'what happened next' cards from stories.json keyExcerpts; cap new cards per day and interleave types. [Size: ~14h]
verification: Unit tests for the scheduler against reference FSRS vectors if adopted; A/B day-7 return rate in PostHog.
